name: Algebra 1 Performance Tasks + Quick Checks Course Profile
authority: Base Performance Tasks + Quick Checks PM owns universal mechanics. This Framework owns Algebra-specific evidence purpose, map expectations, timing/page behavior, action/representation choices, graph-tool use, paths, and all-course scope. Original embedded Assessment Plans remain authoritative for exact I-cans/evidence content.

build_scope.normal_request: all active Units 1-8 in one run

source_intelligence.rule: Use the Assessment Plan first for exact I-cans/evidence. Future-resource hooks and section enrichment are idea/reference seeds, not mandates. They may improve task design but never replace or distort the I-can map.

plan_first_gate.coverage_rule: Map exact I-cans first across the complete requested scope. Read the whole map before rendering and repair accidental I-can gaps, overconcentration, weak evidence, or repeated template choreography before HTML is authored.
plan_first_gate.repetition_discipline: Use the all-course map to distinguish purposeful repetition from template-driven cloning. Repeated Algebra actions/families are allowed when the I-can/evidence job supports them; no anti-repetition quotas. Revise accidental choreography clusters in the PLAN before HTML.

quick_checks.identity: quiz-like deeper evidence that gives a better/bigger picture than an Exit Ticket
quick_checks.independence: student completes independently unless explicit teacher instruction changes this
quick_checks.print_use: US Letter portrait; printed, collected, and scanned for the student portfolio
quick_checks.page_rule: 1 page preferred when honest evidence fits; up to 2 pages allowed. Never split a question card across pages.
quick_checks.workspace_rule: Blank white writing space; no ruled answer lines; Name/Date have open white space rather than underline rules. APPROVED DOUBLED workspace geometry: small 1.40in, medium 2.40in, large 3.60in, xlarge 4.80in; equation-response 1.10in.
quick_checks.visible_alignment: show the exact section I-can statements in a compact Evidence Focus block; do not show DOK/Mastery/internal generator labels beside individual questions
quick_checks.question_count: flexible; normally a small set of substantial evidence opportunities rather than an Exit Ticket pulse or a mini-Summative
quick_checks.coverage_default: For Algebra sections, normally cover all current exact section I-cans when that can be done honestly inside the 8-15 minute target. If not, the map must name which I-cans receive evidence and why others are deferred.
quick_checks.representations: Use Graph / Equation / Table / Context substantively when the I-can supports them. A Quick Check may author a new graph/figure with the Framework graph tool because it is an evidence-authoring resource, not a downstream Bank renderer.

parallel_versions.purpose: Six parallel quiz-like evidence forms per section.
parallel_versions.evidence_rule: Map one section evidence blueprint first. All six versions preserve the same exact I-can coverage, evidence jobs, response mode, approximate difficulty, and 8-15 minute ceiling.
parallel_versions.variation_rule: Versions may change values, names/context details, ordering within tables/choices, or representation particulars when those changes preserve the mapped evidence. Do not invent a new I-can job merely to make a form look different.
parallel_versions.scramble_rule: Scramble the question order across the six versions using planned permutations, then renumber visibly. Do not keep all six in the same order.
parallel_versions.visible_version_label: Show a small Version 1-6 identifier in the footer so collected/scanned forms remain distinguishable; do not place version badges on individual questions.
parallel_versions.single_html_rule: All six complete forms live inside ONE section HTML at u{U}_{S}_quick_check.html. Do not create _v2/_v3/_v4/_v5/_v6 HTML files.
parallel_versions.form_markup: Render six complete sibling form blocks using class="quick-check qc-version" and data-version="1" through "6" (or equivalent semantically clear version attributes). Each form keeps its own header/evidence/questions/footer.
parallel_versions.print_separation: A hard print page break occurs after each version except Version 6 so a new form always starts on a fresh sheet/page.

quick_checks.mathjax_rule: Every visible TeX-style expression must be inside MathJax delimiters. Use the established course-wide dollar-delimiter contract: $...$ inline, $$...$$ display, processEscapes true. This must match the Framework finalizer and MathJax repair tool; do not invent a PT/QC-only delimiter system.
quick_checks.mathjax_exact_head_snippet:
<script>
window.MathJax = {
  tex: {
    inlineMath: [['$','$']],
    displayMath: [['$$','$$']],
    processEscapes: true
  }
};
</script>
<script async src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js"></script>

performance_tasks.identity: richer coherent evidence route; Algebra's primary vehicle for DOK 4 and selected DOK 3 evidence
performance_tasks.dok_rule: Performance Tasks are Algebra's primary DOK 4 vehicle, with selected honest DOK 3 tasks. Design from the I-can/evidence job first, then verify the task actually requires the claimed thinking. DOK remains descriptive metadata and never becomes a proficiency tier or artificial sentence-level add-on.
performance_tasks.evidence_character: One coherent situation/problem/design/model should generate multiple connected pieces of evidence rather than a bundle of unrelated quiz questions.
performance_tasks.independence: Shared setup, data collection, movement, building, or partner exchange may be appropriate. The final mathematical evidence used for portfolio judgment should clearly preserve what the individual student knows/can do when independence matters.
performance_tasks.typical_pages: often 2-4 student pages when the action genuinely needs them; do not pad to a fixed page count
performance_tasks.four_views: Graph / Equation / Table / Context are a high-value Algebra pathway. Frequently connect several or all four when natural, especially in modeling. Do not force all four into an I-can where another representation/action gives stronger evidence.
performance_tasks.modeling_route: A particularly strong Algebra route is collect data -> organize table -> make graph -> find/model an equation by hand and/or with Desmos -> use the model -> test/evaluate/defend it.

action_library.student_does: collect/measure data, organize it, model it, predict, physically or numerically test, and evaluate the model
use movement or position to create data/structure, graph/model it, make a prediction, and validate
construct a pattern/model, count/record structure, generalize, and reason backward from a later result
inspect connected representations/claims, locate a mismatch, repair it, test the repair, and defend the corrected model
create a valid representation/model, exchange evidence, reconstruct missing information, evaluate equivalence, and revise
model alternatives/constraints, compare outcomes, optimize or choose, and justify a recommendation
analyze supplied or collected data, select/build a model, validate it, and explain limitations

performance_tasks.balance_rule: Do not let the course collapse into only data-collection/model-fit tasks. The all-course map should deliberately include strong audit/repair and create/reconstruct/evaluate performances where the I-cans support them, alongside modeling/building/movement/decision tasks. This is a thinking-balance check, not a rotation quota.
performance_tasks.graph_tool: May generate student evidence, comparison graphs, data displays, or teacher-guide/reference visuals when supported. If graph construction is itself the evidence, give students the blank/appropriate scaffold instead of pre-solving it.
performance_tasks.teacher_guide: Required for every Performance Task. It is a page-for-page replica of the student document using the same CSS. Put answers, sample answers, acceptable reasoning, or evaluation criteria in RED inside the same workspace where the student writes. Do not replace the student-facing task with a separate answer-key layout.
performance_tasks.css_scope_rule: Use the same performance_task.css across Algebra Performance Task actions. It is a shared course-root stylesheet at css/performance_task.css, not a copy inside the Performance Task resource root. A different course Framework may explicitly adapt/select a different course-specific presentation when its evidence structures require it.
performance_tasks.dok_course_balance_rule: Across an all-course build, DOK 4 should be a major/dominant role because this resource family is the course vehicle for extended thinking. DOK 3 remains appropriate where the section I-cans do not honestly support DOK 4. A map with only a tiny handful of DOK 4 tasks is a PLAN FAILURE unless the Assessment Plans provide a compelling reason. Do not enforce a numeric quota or inflate DOK with generic reflection.
performance_tasks.render_from_action_rule: Stable performance_task.css controls visual language only. Page count, task-card count, headings, materials, shared/individual structure, and student sequence must follow the mapped action. All/near-all tasks rendering as the same 2-page/5-card shell is a render-fidelity failure unless the map genuinely requires it.
performance_tasks.action_fidelity_rule: The action name is a promise: CREATE/TRADE requires an actual exchange/reconstruction/evaluation mechanism; MOVE requires actual movement/setup; COLLECT requires actual data collection/recording; BUILD requires construction; AUDIT/REPAIR requires a real inconsistency; ANALYZE DATASET requires an actual dataset. Do not label a text worksheet with an action whose core verbs never occur.
performance_tasks.representation_fidelity_rule: If a prompt says a grid/table/diagram/data display is provided, include it. If graph/model construction is itself evidence, provide a practical scaffold unless the task explicitly uses external graph paper/tooling.
performance_tasks.mathjax_rule: Every visible TeX-style expression must be inside MathJax delimiters. Use the established course-wide dollar-delimiter contract: $...$ inline, $$...$$ display, processEscapes true. This must match the Framework finalizer and MathJax repair tool; do not invent a PT/QC-only delimiter system.

package.quick_check: quick_check____htq5855/u{U}_{S}_quick_check/u{U}_{S}_quick_check.html — the ONE HTML contains all six complete versions.
package.figures: figures/ inside the section folder only when needed
package.css_packaging_rule: Do NOT package CSS inside performance_task___5134zrt/ or quick_check____htq5855/. Those stylesheets live in the existing course-root css/ folder. The returned all-course resource ZIP still contains exactly the two obscured resource folders; section HTML links ../../css/performance_task.css or ../../css/quick_check.css.
package.quick_check_single_html: Exactly one Quick Check HTML per active section; that one file contains Versions 1-6.

qa_before_delivery: Every requested active section appears in both maps and final folder trees.
Every exact I-can is intentionally considered before authoring; accidental coverage gaps are repaired or explicitly justified in the map.
Quick Checks remain independent, roughly 8-15 minutes, 1-2 pages, and no question card is split by printing.
Performance Tasks are coherent performances rather than bundles of unrelated questions and genuinely contain the intended DOK 3/4 reasoning after design.
All-course Performance Task actions show meaningful balance; audit/repair and create/reconstruct/evaluate opportunities are not accidentally absent when suitable.
Graph/Equation/Table/Context work is real when claimed; decorative representations do not count.
Student-facing figures have no descriptive captions beneath them; prompts introduce representations and necessary labels stay inside the representation.
Every Performance Task teacher guide mirrors its student document and uses red answer/sample-answer text inside student workspaces.
Only the two exact obscured resource roots occur at the top of the returned ZIP.
No __MACOSX/.DS_Store files and no broken relative CSS/figure links.
All six Quick Check versions preserve the mapped I-can/evidence blueprint, use planned variation, and do not all use the same question order.
Quick Check blank workspace uses the approved doubled geometry and whole question cards still do not split across printed pages.
Visible TeX-style mathematics in both resource families is inside MathJax delimiters and renders as mathematical notation rather than raw caret/underscore text.
Performance Task all-course DOK distribution reflects the resource family's primary DOK 4 role with selected honest DOK 3; a tiny DOK 4 minority triggers plan repair.
Performance Task page/card/headings/materials follow the mapped action; a universal 2-page/5-card shell across the course is not accepted merely because the CSS is shared.
Action labels match actual student behavior; create/trade, move, collect, build, audit/repair, and dataset actions are literal when named.
If a prompt promises a provided grid/table/diagram/data display, the object actually exists.
No .css file is packaged inside either obscured returned resource root; HTML links the shared course-root css files with ../../css/... .
Each active section contains exactly ONE Quick Check HTML file, and that file contains exactly six complete printable version blocks; no _v2 through _v6 HTML files exist.
The exact approved MathJax head snippet is present on mathematical PT/QC HTML; display delimiters are configured under displayMath, never as a second inlineMath pair.
